subject: Hiring budget reallocation and temporary offer pause — guidance and exceptions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Hiring Managers <hiring-managers@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hiring budget reallocation and temporary offer pause — guidance and exceptions

Team,

Quick update from finance/product planning: we need a temporary, company-wide hiring credit reallocation to hit Q2 operating targets. Effective immediately, all outbound offers should be paused for non-exempt roles until we finalize an updated headcount plan.

Please action the following today:
- Stop any offer signings that are not already accepted and scheduled to start within the next 10 business days.
- Send me (soojin) a one-line note for any candidate you believe is mission-critical with a short justification (impact, revenue/ops risk) + requested start date.
- Attach the role's band and the requested compensation (total).

We will run a rapid exception review with finance/HR and leadership. Exception criteria will prioritize customer-facing revenue lifts, critical infra/security hires, and legally bound start dates.

I know this is disruptive — recruiting/people ops will work with hiring teams to present pragmatic alternatives (deferred starts, reduced sign-on, contractor bridging). Please do not rescind accepted offers until we confirm exception status.

I will compile requests and circulate by EOD tomorrow so we can decide before the next sprint planning cycle.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Talent & People Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Q2_headcount_reforecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hiring budget reallocation and temporary offer pause — guidance and exceptions

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 09:15, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> Quick update from finance/product planning: we need a temporary, company-wide hiring credit reallocation to hit Q2 operating targets....

Soojin — appreciate the heads up. I have one time-sensitive case: Daniel Park (candidate) verbally accepted our offer for Senior Infra Engineer last week and we delivered an official offer (attached). He is planning to give notice at his current employer tomorrow and hopes to start 05/03. Candidate is a top-of-funnel refactor expert for our KV cache work; product and infra leadership flagged him as high impact.

Options I see:
1) Allow a one-time exception and honor the existing offer as-is (preferred if leadership OK).
2) Offer to delay the start by 3–4 weeks to allow paperwork to be paused while still keeping the candidate warm.
3) Convert to a 60-day contractor engagement with intention to convert (will cost more short-term).

I've attached the offer PDF and the role's comp band. If we need an exception, please advise the approvers list — I can send the formal ask tonight.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Product Recruiting
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Offer_DanielPark_v1.pdf (offer letter for Daniel Park)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hiring budget reallocation and temporary offer pause — guidance and exceptions

Thanks for flagging, Soojin and Marissa. High level from finance: we support a temporary pause to give us runway on Q2 margin targets, but we must avoid actions that create legal or candidate-experience risk.

Guidance:
- Do not rescind fully executed offers; for verbal-only acceptances, exceptions are allowed but must be routed through the exception committee (me + soojin + lauren) and include a clear offset (e.g., swap a headcount from another non-critical req or show near-term customer revenue linked to the hire).
- Any exception approved must be paired with a documented cost mitigation (deferred hire elsewhere or reduced contractor spend).
- For start dates within 10 business days, default to approving (we will fund temporarily) but we need written confirmation from the hiring manager signed off by Lauren.

Marissa: please submit a 1‑page exception form for Daniel with the items above. We'll triage first thing Monday.

Vivek
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hiring budget reallocation and temporary offer pause — guidance and exceptions

Folks — adding recruiting perspective and quick mitigation playbook so teams can move fast without damaging candidate experience:

Candidate scenarios and suggested actions:
- Accepted + notice given (start < 14 days): push for exception approval; present start date evidence; offer interim contractor or sign-on deferral instead of rescind.
- Verbal acceptance, no paperwork: place offer "on hold" and keep candidate engaged with regular touchpoints; explicit transparency wins over silence.
- Extended pipeline (offers not yet extended): pause new offers and redirect requisitions to contract requisition where possible.

I've created a shared worksheet with each open req, current stage, and proposed mitigation. Link: https://docs.redwood.com/ds/Q2-headcount-reforecast (view-only). I'll also flag candidate vulnerability scores so hiring managers know who needs urgent attention.

If Marissa wants me to draft the 1-page exception request for Daniel, I can do that now and copy the committee.

— Priyom
Head of Technical Recruiting
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hiring budget reallocation and temporary offer pause — guidance and exceptions

Thank you everyone for the quick coordination and the mitigation options. After reviewing the spreadsheet and hearing the committee, here is the decision:

1) Temporary pause is approved effective immediately for all new offers outside of the exceptions process. This pause remains in effect until we publish the updated Q2 headcount reforecast (target: EOD Fri).

2) One-time exceptions: we will approve the Daniel Park exception. Rationale: critical infra skill set + verified start within 10 business days + product impact tied to a customer milestone. Marissa — please submit the 1-page exception form and include the offset you propose (swap with an open non-critical req or fund from the contractor budget). Once I sign, Priyom can proceed with onboarding scheduling.

3) Process note: any other exception requests must route through the committee (soojin + vivek + lauren) and reference SUP-1234 for tracking. Approved exceptions must be logged in the Q2 workbook and include a budget offset.

4) No offers to be rescinded. If a candidate asks for confirmation and we have not approved an exception, be transparent and offer deferred start alternatives rather than silence.

I'll sign Marissa's form as soon as it's in my inbox. Thanks for keeping candidate experience front and center while we fix the books.

— Lauren
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
